msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all structural components of a typical Multipolar Neurone: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Cell body Cyton / Soma
B) Receptive Dendrites
C) Axon Hillock and conducting Axon
D) Terminal arborization with Synaptic Knobs
E) Contractile Sarcomeres
answers: A) Cell body Cyton / Soma
B) Receptive Dendrites
C) Axon Hillock and conducting Axon
D) Terminal arborization with Synaptic Knobs
msqs.explanation: Neurone structure = Cyton, Dendrites, Axon Hillock, Axon, and Synaptic Knobs.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all neuroglial cells residing in the Central Nervous System (CNS): (Select all that apply)
options: A) Astrocytes
B) Oligodendrocytes
C) Microglia
D) Ependymal cells
E) Schwann cells
answers: A) Astrocytes
B) Oligodendrocytes
C) Microglia
D) Ependymal cells
msqs.explanation: CNS neuroglia: Astrocytes, Oligodendrocytes, Microglia, Ependymal. Schwann = PNS.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all neuroglial cells residing in the Peripheral Nervous System (PNS): (Select all that apply)
options: A) Myelinating Schwann cells
B) Ganglionic Satellite cells
C) CNS Astrocytes
D) CNS Microglia
E) CNS Oligodendrocytes
answers: A) Myelinating Schwann cells
B) Ganglionic Satellite cells
msqs.explanation: PNS neuroglia include Schwann cells and Satellite cells.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all functions of Astrocytes in the brain: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Form Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) perivascular feet
B) Regulate extracellular K+ ion concentration
C) Take up excess neurotransmitters (Glutamate)
D) Provide structural metabolic support to neurones
E) Synthesize PNS myelin sheath
answers: A) Form Blood-Brain Barrier (BBB) perivascular feet
B) Regulate extracellular K+ ion concentration
C) Take up excess neurotransmitters (Glutamate)
D) Provide structural metabolic support to neurones
msqs.explanation: Astrocytes form BBB, regulate K+ and glutamate, and provide metabolic support.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all features of Saltatory Nerve Conduction in myelinated axons: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Leaping impulse propagation from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier
B) High conduction velocity (up to 120 m/s)
C) High concentration of voltage-gated Na+ channels at Nodes
D) Energy conservation due to restricted Na+/K+ ATP pumping
E) Continuous slow uninsulated axolemma wave depolarization
answers: A) Leaping impulse propagation from Node of Ranvier to Node of Ranvier
B) High conduction velocity (up to 120 m/s)
C) High concentration of voltage-gated Na+ channels at Nodes
D) Energy conservation due to restricted Na+/K+ ATP pumping
msqs.explanation: Saltatory conduction is fast, leaps node to node, saves ATP, and relies on high Na+ channel density at nodes.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all anatomical locations containing Bipolar Neurones: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Retina of eye
B) Olfactory mucosa of nose
C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
D) Cerebral cortex
E) Dorsal root ganglion
answers: A) Retina of eye
B) Olfactory mucosa of nose
C) Inner ear vestibular and cochlear organs
msqs.explanation: Bipolar neurones occur in retina, olfactory mucosa, and inner ear.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all features characteristic of Nissl's Granules: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Composed of Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and Ribosomes
B) Active site of protein synthesis in neurones
C) Present in Cyton and Dendrites
D) Strictly ABSENT in Axon and Axon Hillock
E) Present in high density inside axon terminal knobs
answers: A) Composed of Rough Endoplasmic Reticulum and Ribosomes
B) Active site of protein synthesis in neurones
C) Present in Cyton and Dendrites
D) Strictly ABSENT in Axon and Axon Hillock
msqs.explanation: Nissl's granules (RER + ribosomes) synthesize protein in cyton and dendrites, but are absent in axon/axon hillock.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all steps involved in Chemical Synaptic Transmission: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Action potential reaches presynaptic axon terminal
B) Influx of Ca2+ ions through voltage-gated channels
C) Exocytosis of synaptic vesicles releasing neurotransmitters into synaptic cleft
D) Neurotransmitter binding to postsynaptic receptors altering membrane potential
E) Reverse nerve conduction from axon back to dendrite
answers: A) Action potential reaches presynaptic axon terminal
B) Influx of Ca2+ ions through voltage-gated channels
C) Exocytosis of synaptic vesicles releasing neurotransmitters into synaptic cleft
D) Neurotransmitter binding to postsynaptic receptors altering membrane potential
msqs.explanation: Synaptic transmission involves action potential arrival, Ca2+ influx, neurotransmitter exocytosis, and receptor binding.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all neurone structural classifications based on neurite process count: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Unipolar (Single axon, no dendrites - Embryo)
B) Bipolar (One axon, one dendrite - Retina)
C) Multipolar (One axon, multiple dendrites - Brain)
D) Pseudounipolar (Single process dividing into 2 branches - DRG)
E) Apolar / Anaxonic (No true axon - Amacrine cells)
answers: A) Unipolar (Single axon, no dendrites - Embryo)
B) Bipolar (One axon, one dendrite - Retina)
C) Multipolar (One axon, multiple dendrites - Brain)
D) Pseudounipolar (Single process dividing into 2 branches - DRG)
E) Apolar / Anaxonic (No true axon - Amacrine cells)
msqs.explanation: Neurone structural types include Unipolar, Bipolar, Multipolar, Pseudounipolar, and Anaxonic.

msqs.stem: From Question Bank perspective, in Topic 5, select all functions performed by Ependymal Neuroglial cells: (Select all that apply)
options: A) Line ventricles of brain and central canal of spinal cord
B) Possess apical cilia to facilitate Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) circulation
C) Form choroid plexus tissue producing CSF
D) Act as neural stem cells in specialized neurogenic niches
E) Form peripheral nerve myelin sheath
answers: A) Line ventricles of brain and central canal of spinal cord
B) Possess apical cilia to facilitate Cerebrospinal Fluid (CSF) circulation
C) Form choroid plexus tissue producing CSF
D) Act as neural stem cells in specialized neurogenic niches
msqs.explanation: Ependymal cells line CNS ventricles/canal, possess cilia for CSF circulation, form choroid plexus, and serve as neural progenitors.
